title: Review: getting to know someone
topic: unit review: regular present, ser, tener, questions
why: Review of the first unit, with nothing new: you bring together ser, tener, the three groups of regular verbs and question words to introduce yourself in detail and ask someone about themselves. It's the full conversation of a first language exchange, which wraps up the "Introducing yourself" unit.

The present: everything you already know

Well done, you've finished your first unit! This lesson brings no new rules: it puts everything together so you can introduce yourself in detail and ask someone about themselves.

The two pillars

sertener

túerestienes

The three regular groups

hablarcomervivir
yohablocomovivo
túhablascomesvives
él, ella, ustedhablacomevive
nosotros, nosotrashablamoscomemosvivimos
vosotros, vosotrashabláiscoméisvivís
ellos, ellas, ustedeshablancomenviven

Three reflexes to keep:

  • the subject is dropped most of the time, unlike in English: Vivo en Lyon;
  • the negative is one word, before the verb, with no \"do\": No trabajo los sábados;
  • a yes/no question keeps the normal word order and is written between ¿ and ?: ¿Hablas inglés?

For a habit, use the plural article: los sábados (on Saturdays, every Saturday), los fines de semana (on weekends, every weekend).

", "

Introducing yourself in detail

Here's a complete introduction, sentence by sentence. Read it out loud, then replace the details with your own.

¡Hola! Me llamo Ana y soy francesa, de Toulouse.Hello! My name is Ana and I'm French, from Toulouse.
Tengo treinta años.I'm thirty.
Vivo en Madrid y soy ingeniera. Trabajo en una oficina.I live in Madrid and I'm an engineer. I work in an office.
Hablo francés, inglés y un poco de español.I speak French, English and a little Spanish.
Los fines de semana leo, cocino y bailo. A veces corro en el parque.On weekends, I read, cook and dance. Sometimes I run in the park.

Questions for getting to know someone

To ask about…You say
their name¿Cómo te llamas?
where they're from¿De dónde eres?
their age¿Cuántos años tienes?
their city¿Dónde vives?
their job¿A qué te dedicas? ¿Dónde trabajas?
their languages¿Qué idiomas hablas?
their reason¿Por qué aprendes español?
their hobbies¿Lees? ¿Cocinas? ¿Practicas deporte?

For hobbies, you don't know the verbs for likes and dislikes yet: just ask yes/no questions with regular verbs. Practicar deporte = to play sports, to exercise.

To react naturally: ¡Qué bien! (great!), ¡Qué interesante! (how interesting!), ¿Y tú? (and you?). And at the end: Encantado if you're a man, Encantada if you're a woman.

", "

The unit's traps

These are the mistakes English speakers make most often at the start. Read them again before the exercises.

WrongRightWhy
Soy treinta años.Tengo treinta años.Age uses tener, not \"to be\".
Soy una periodista.Soy periodista.A job takes no article (no \"a\").
Soy Francés.Soy francés.Nationalities are lowercase.
Yo soy Ana. Yo vivo en Lyon.Soy Ana. Vivo en Lyon.The subject is usually dropped.
vivemos, viveisvivimos, vivís-ir verbs keep the i.
¿Donde trabajas?¿Dónde trabajas?Question words have an accent.
—¿Por qué? —Por qué…—¿Por qué? —Porque…The answer is written as one word.
Hablo no inglés.No hablo inglés.No goes before the verb.

Agreement to watch

  • Nationalities agree, like adjectives: un amigo francés, una amiga francesa, unos amigos franceses.
  • Cuánto agrees with the noun: ¿Cuántos idiomas hablas?, ¿Cuántas hermanas tienes?
  • A mixed group takes the masculine plural: Ana y Javier son españoles.
—¿Cuántos idiomas hablas? —Hablo tres idiomas: francés, inglés y español.—How many languages do you speak? —I speak three languages: French, English and Spanish.

The best practice: introduce yourself out loud every day in one minute, then ask yourself the questions from the previous table as if you were meeting someone.
